rendering.persona_description: Gustavo is a 34-year-old transgender man who edits audio for a couple of small podcast networks, working mostly from his apartment. He grew up in a mid-sized city, has one younger sister he talks to most weeks, and spends his downtime restoring an old mountain bike he never quite finishes fixing. He is quick and funny in writing but far more guarded out loud, especially with anyone he doesn't already trust.
rendering.clinical_context: Gustavo has had social anxiety since middle school, focused on being watched, judged, or laughed at when he speaks in front of others; it sharpened again in his late twenses around coming out and starting testosterone, when he became hyper-alert to being stared at or misread in public. He's currently five months into exposure-based CBT, working through a hierarchy that includes phone calls, ordering in person, and speaking up in client meetings. He's been telling his therapist he might be done with it, though he hasn't cancelled the next session yet.
rendering.behavioral_description: Gustavo answers in short, flat sentences and gets sharper or more sarcastic when he feels steered. He'll mention a specific bad moment, like freezing on a client call, but downplays it right after, and if he's told what to do he'll argue the opposite side just to see if it holds up. He asks pointed questions to test whether the person talking to him actually knows anything, and he's more likely to argue with a suggestion than to say he's scared.
